situation:
You are the human resources director at MERIDIAN FORGE SOFTWARE, a co-operative owned by the people who work in it. The general manager (judge), elected by the member-owners, has asked you to recommend how the co-operative should fund the wage increase its members approved last month, and to explain the recommendation to the membership.

The co-operative writes scheduling software for hospitals and has grown from forty member-owners to a hundred and ten in two years. Members vote on pay policy, and this spring they voted to raise the base wage by eight percent across every role. The vote set the raise; it did not say where the money comes from, and that decision sits with the general manager (judge).

Two sources are available and neither is free. The co-operative could pause this year's patronage dividend, the share of profit it pays every member each December, which would cover the raise in full this quarter. Members count on that payment and would lose it for the year, and the co-operative recruits on it: candidates are told they will own a share of what they build.

The other source is hiring. Twelve open roles are funded and unfilled, and leaving them open for two quarters pays for the raise without touching the dividend. The work those roles were meant to carry falls on members who are already at capacity, and the co-operative has delivery dates with three hospital clients in the next quarter that it would be staffing short.

The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on which source funds the raise, and how you would present that choice to the member-owners who voted for it. You will present your recommendation to the general manager (judge) in the general manager's office. The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of general manager (judge) of MERIDIAN FORGE SOFTWARE, a co-operative owned by the people who work in it.

Business background is the same as the situation above. The members voted to raise the base wage by eight percent across every role without saying where the money comes from, and the two sources available are this year's patronage dividend and the twelve funded roles that are still unfilled.

You have asked the human resources director (participant) to recommend which source funds the raise, and how that choice is presented to the member-owners who voted for it.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we go your way, what does the choice we did not take cost us?
What would have to happen for you to change your recommendation?
